questions.title: Who will Ghana appoint to lead the Black Stars for the September–October 2026 international window?
questions.background: The Black Stars are Ghana's senior men's national football team.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The Ghana Football Association's official announcement appointing a head coach for the international window running from September 21 to October 6, 2026, corroborated by reliable news reporting. Resolution Condition : Resolve to the first person appointed after August 1, 2026, and before the international window begins, to lead the team during that window. Both interim and permanent appointments qualify. Accepted Answer Format : The appointed coach's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Breaking Aug 26 Ghanaian reports (Ghana Sports Page exclusive echoed by MyNewsGh) cite GFA sources saying the association is set to appoint current Black Stars assistant and former U20/U23 coach Desmond Ofei as head coach ahead of the Sept 24 AFCON 2027 qualifier vs Cote d'Ivoire, 'if nothing major changes in the coming few days.' This aligns with last week's Carlos Queiroz ~$150k/month salary impasse and urgent squad call-up timeline. Because the appointment is not yet officially confirmed by the GFA, we cap Ofei at 0.54 (up from 0.41) while cutting Queiroz 0.31 -> 0.21 in case last-minute Ministry of Sports intervention resolves the deadlock, nudging local alternative Maxwell Konadu to 0.04 and leaving 16.5% on the broader field.
watch_keywords: Ghana Football Association Black Stars head coach

questions.title: Which Israeli cabinet minister, if any, will unveil a named plan to remove Gaza's entire Palestinian population during the first week of September 2026?
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Public statements by Israeli cabinet ministers, documented in contemporaneous reporting by established news organizations. Qualifying Event : Between September 1 and September 7, 2026, inclusive, a serving Israeli cabinet minister must publicly introduce an explicitly named plan for removing Gaza's Palestinian population from the territory. General endorsements of population removal or proposals for evacuating particular areas within Gaza do not qualify. Implementation is not required. Accepted Answer Format : Provide the minister's full name, or “None” if no qualifying announcement occurs.
questions.current_reasoning: Major Aug 27-30 Israeli campaign developments in local Times of Israel and Arab News coverage strengthen Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich as the #1 candidate entering the Sept 1-7 qualifying window: (1) On Aug 27—exactly two months before the Oct 27 election—Smotrich demonstrated his exact named-plan campaign playbook by unveiling an explicitly named master plan ('Yes, Judaization' for the Negev and Galilee) paired with a provocative AI video; (2) A Aug 27 Zman Yisrael poll showed ex-general Ofer Winter's new People of Israel party surging to 6 seats (explicitly campaigning on 'voluntary emigration from Gaza') while pushing Smotrich's Religious Zionism below the 3.25% Knesset threshold; and (3) On Aug 28 Itamar Ben-Gvir flatly refused Netanyahu's demand to merge with Smotrich, leaving Smotrich fighting for political survival in merger talks with <1% Zehut's Moshe Feiglin and with peak incentive to unveil a named Gaza removal plan as September begins. Meanwhile, Defense Minister Israel Katz remains #2 via the Gaza emigration directorate (0.25 -> 0.22), Ben-Gvir (polling safely at 6-8 seats, focusing on viral stunts such as his Aug 30 prison video) trims 0.18 -> 0.16, Gila Gamliel trims 0.04 -> 0.025 while bogged down in a Likud primary recount fight after dropping to #35 (Aug 29 ToI), and 'None' holds near 0.19 (0.20 -> 0.19) respecting the strict 7-day explicitly named full-removal criteria (sum = 0.935, leaving 6.5% for other serving cabinet ministers).

questions.title: Which Southeast Asian country will declare a state of emergency over wildfire haze between September 1 and September 5, 2026?
questions.background: Seasonal wildfire smoke can cross borders in Southeast Asia, creating public-health risks and prompting emergency government responses.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official national government announcements, corroborated by reliable news reporting. Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the country whose national authorities announce a formal state of emergency because of wildfire haze between September 1 and September 5, 2026, inclusive. The declaration may cover the entire country or a specific area within it. Air-quality warnings, school closures, or health advisories without a formal emergency declaration do not qualify. Accepted Answer Format : The country’s common English name.
questions.current_reasoning: Hard 2026-08-31 official API data and government announcements (Bernama, The Star, Malay Mail, DayakDaily, CNA) sharply strengthen Malaysia entering tomorrow's Sept 1-5 qualifying window. First, Sarawak's Serian API jumped from 436 (Aug 30) to 476 at 8am, 475 at 9-10am, 463 at noon, and 456 at 1pm on Aug 31—just 24 points below Malaysia's statutory 500 emergency trigger—while six other Sarawak localities hit hazardous >300 readings (Tebedu 409, Lubok Antu 387, Lundu 381, Kuching 349, Samarahan 336, Sri Aman 331). Second, Malaysia did NOT declare early on Aug 31 (removing premature-declaration risk): Deputy Premier / SDMC chairman Douglas Uggah Embas explicitly announced Monday afternoon that no emergency is needed yet, but once any area hits API 500 it will be escalated to federal NADMA in Kuala Lumpur for a localized emergency declaration under NADMA Directive No. 1 (matching the resolution criteria's localized national-authority clause), and Sarawak's cloud seeding is not scheduled until Sept 3-5 while 324+ Kalimantan hotspots continue driving dense smoke north. Third, an Aug 29-31 Indonesia check shows zero national state of emergency movement, with BNPB noting cloud seeding induced light-to-moderate rain in parts of Sumatra and West Kalimantan (CNA Aug 29). Raising Malaysia 0.64 -> 0.76 (below 0.85 to respect risk that Serian peaks below 500 or Jakarta declares a national haze emergency) and lowering Indonesia 0.31 -> 0.20, with Brunei 0.015 (dense smoke reported over Brunei on Aug 31), Singapore 0.015, Thailand 0.005 (sum = 0.995).

questions.title: Which bank will the U.S. Treasury sanction over alleged financial ties to Iran during August 31–September 6, 2026?
questions.background: The United States uses financial sanctions to restrict institutions accused of helping Iran access the international financial system.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official U.S. Treasury sanctions announcements and Office of Foreign Assets Control designation records. Resolution Conditions : Identify the bank newly sanctioned during August 31–September 6, 2026, for allegedly facilitating financial transactions for Iran. Resolve when the Treasury publicly announces the designation. Accepted Answer Format : The bank's commonly used name.
questions.current_reasoning: Refined ahead of the Aug 31-Sept 6 window using 2026-08-28/29 reporting (Iran International, Sullivan & Cromwell, AP News, Khaleej Times, Arab News). Following FinCEN's Aug 28 Section 311 proposed rule on Banque Misr UAE (outside the Aug 31-Sept 6 window, with the UAE Central Bank launching an urgent forensic probe on Aug 29), Iran International (Aug 29) confirms two critical targeting points: (1) Turkey's Halkbank already ended its decade-long US criminal case earlier this year via a deal barring Iran business touching the US and Turkish banks are avoiding Iran-linked payments—removing Halkbank (0.02 -> 0); (2) Washington views Dubai and Baghdad—not Beijing—as Iran's primary usable hard-currency corridors, with Iraq pressure focused on policing USD correspondent channels and cutting off Iraqi banks moving money for Iran and its militias. Accordingly, we lift Iraq's most scrutinized state bank Rafidain Bank (0.10 -> 0.11), hold Trade Bank of Iraq (0.045) and Rasheed Bank (0.035), add Iraq's leading vetted private USD-correspondent bank National Bank of Iraq (0.02), and trim Bank of China (0.02 -> 0.015) given repeated reporting of US reluctance to hit major Chinese G-SIBs, keeping total top-5 mass disciplined at 0.225.

questions.title: Who will score the opening goal when Real Betis host Real Madrid in La Liga in September 2026?
questions.background: The opening goalscorer is the player officially credited with the first goal of the match.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : La Liga's official match record, corroborated by reliable match reporting. Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the player credited with the earliest goal in the September 2026 La Liga fixture hosted by Real Betis against Real Madrid. Disallowed goals do not count. If the match finishes goalless, resolve as “No goalscorer.” Accepted Answer Format : The player's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Updated on Sunday 2026-08-30 local coverage (Al Jazeera, Irish Times) after Real Madrid's 4-0 rout of Malaga ahead of Friday Sept 4's trip to Real Betis. Jude Bellingham opened the scoring in the 19th minute with a solo burst—his second opening goal in three La Liga starts under Jose Mourinho (also 9' opener at Espanyol)—then headed the rebound that forced Malaga's 26th-minute own goal and struck the post at 55', justifying a sharp upward revision (0.085 -> 0.115) alongside Vinicius Junior (0.12 -> 0.115, assisted Arda Guler's late 4th goal). Kylian Mbappe netted a 30th-minute volley to reach 4 goals in 3 league matches and nudges up (0.23 -> 0.24). With Real Madrid scoring 10 goals in 3 matches (even after Mourinho rotated five starters) and Betis coming off a 5-2 defensive collapse at Levante, a 0-0 draw ('No goalscorer') trims further (0.055 -> 0.045). For Betis, Estadio Deportivo gave Troy Parrott a harsh 4/10 after missing a clear second-half header at Levante before being subbed at 57', trimming Parrott slightly (0.055 -> 0.045) on mild rotation risk vs Cucho Hernandez; total top-5 mass = 0.56.
watch_keywords: Real Betis Real Madrid lineup injury

questions.title: Which commodity category will record the largest monthly percentage price increase in the FAO Food Price Index for August 2026?
questions.background: The UN Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) publishes a monthly index tracking international prices across major food commodity categories.
questions.resolution_criteria: Resolve to the commodity category with the largest percentage price increase from July to August 2026, as reported in the FAO's September 2026 Food Price Index release. Resolution Date: 2026-09-04 Answer with the category name.
questions.current_reasoning: With August trading effectively complete on 2026-08-31, end-of-month commodity summaries from Saxo (Aug 28) and Bloomberg / Daily Caller / NewsBytes (Aug 31) cement Sugar as the dominant FAO Food Price Index gainer for August ahead of Friday's Sept 4 release. Saxo explicitly calls sugar 'the standout performer, gaining close to 25% this month' and Bloomberg (Aug 31) reports New York raw sugar futures rose roughly 20% in August—their largest monthly gain since 2015—sustaining double-digit gains throughout the month (+19.47% MoM already by Aug 24) that translate directly into FAO's monthly-average ISA Sugar index. By contrast, grains rose ~13% overall (corn +15.6%, while wheat jumped +12.1% only in the final week after sitting -3.44% MoM through Aug 24), heavily damping FAO's full-month Cereals average alongside ~26%-weighted rice (~+1.7%); cocoa (~+20%) is excluded from the 5 FAO FFPI categories. Raising Sugar 0.86 -> 0.90 and trimming Cereals (0.08 -> 0.055), Vegetable Oils (0.04 -> 0.03), Dairy (0.01 -> 0.008), and Meat (0.01 -> 0.007) while retaining a 10% calibration buffer for July base-effect and physical FOB quote divergence (sum = 1.000).
